title: Quarterly Runbook-to-Production: Dedicated Pool Canary Framework & Cost-SLO Lab
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver a repeatable 'Runbook-to-Production' flow for Dedicated capacity changes that combines a Canary Framework, controlled reservation hedging experiments, and a Cost-SLO Lab so product, infra, and SRE can validate autoscale policies against real traffic and cost targets before full rollout.

Context: We frequently iterate on autoscale policies and reservation commitments but lack a lightweight, repeatable pipeline that moves a new autoscale policy from staging rehearsals to customer-facing Dedicated pools with clear rollback criteria. This initiative packages orchestration playbooks, test harnesses, dashboards, and a small-batch canary release pattern so we can validate latency SLOs, tail-percentile behavior, and unit cost effects under controlled load.

Scope:
- Define a canary release pattern for Dedicated pools (staged traffic percentages, sizing of canary pools, KV-cache priming).
- Build Cost-SLO Lab dashboards and automated comparisons against baseline (per-token cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, failed-request ratio).
- Create a runbook with automated checkpoints and decision gates (hand-off to Ops, automatic rollback triggers).
- Integrate reservation hedging window tests (short-term reservation top-ups to test capacity elasticity).
- Produce a reusable 'staging rehearsal' job that runs synthetic and sampled real traffic through new autoscale policies.

Why now: Q1 priority for Dedicated stability and reducing surprise cost/performance regressions following model/quantization changes. Shipping this runbook reduces time-to-rollout for safer, measurable autoscale experiments and supports commercial Reserved Capacity sales by improving predictability.

Deliverables: PRD + runbook doc, canary orchestration templates, Cost-SLO Lab Grafana dashboards, staging rehearsal job and sample dataset, acceptance criteria and rollback templates, rollout retrospective template.
acceptance_criteria: Canary framework can be configured and executed from Console with a single button and a saved policy template
Cost-SLO Lab shows delta vs. baseline for unit cost and p95 latency within 10 minutes of canary start
Runbook automated gates include: p95 latency increase > 15% OR error rate > 0.5% => automatic rollback
Rehearsal job executes with sampled production traffic and produces a quantitative report (latency, cost, KV hit rate)
Two internal teams (SRE and Dedicated infra) have walked the runbook and signed off on rollback criteria

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Canary leaks more traffic than planned and impacts customers -> Mitigation: enforce traffic shaping policy in front of pools and a kill-switch at the loadbalancer level
Risk: Cost metrics lag or are noisy during short canaries -> Mitigation: use aggregated token-level accounting and bootstrap baselines from synthetic replay to reduce noise
Risk: KV cache priming causes bursty backend load -> Mitigation: introduce gradual prefix priming and monitor backend QPS with soft throttles
Risk: Dependencies on infra features (elastic reservation APIs) delay runway -> Mitigation: scope a fallback manual hedging procedure for pilot and schedule dependency delivery with ENG-19345
